---
title: "References"
subtitle: "In-text citations and the reference list"
bibliography: references.bib
link-citations: true
---

A knowledge-node page cites the claim in the sentence and keeps the full
record at the end. This specimen uses Quarto's citation syntax. It is not a
scientific article, and it does not document an SCQ topic.

A literature review is a selection, not a dump of everything read
[@pautasso2013]. Software that produces a result needs a citable identity of
its own [@smith2016]. The sentence can name two sources without turning into a
bracket list.

The reading measure still comes from the same tools that set type. Knuth's
*TeXbook* fixes the box model this page inherits [@knuth1984], Lamport's
manual is the document syntax most scientific pages still assume
[@lamport1994], and Bringhurst states the typographic limits a theme should
not invent around [@bringhurst2004].

Quarto turns `@key` and `[@key]` into links when `link-citations` is set
[@quartoCitations]. Pandoc builds the list and the backlinks
[@pandocCitations]. A long title stays in the list rather than in the heading:
the house style manual is cited here, and its full name belongs below
[@chicago2017].

## Limits

The theme keeps a long identifier, DOI, or URL inside the measure by allowing
it to wrap. It does not restyle the reference list's hanging indent.

Put a few citations in a sentence, not a cluster in every clause. The list
belongs at the end of the page. A heading should name the claim; it should
not carry the bibliography.
